LESSON: READING 4.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READERS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.4: Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers, part of Strand 4 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What would you consider when selecting a storybook to read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the main characters in a text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain how the characters make the story flow,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. make predictions based on the title and the sections read,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role of characters in the class reader.  Read a section of a class reader and identify the main characters,  Discuss predictions made from the title and the sections read. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views. What would you consider when selecting a storybook to read? 36  Participate in a reader’s theatre and read portions of the class reader. Create a conducive environment and adequate space for learners with mobility difficulties and ensure safety for all learners as they perform the activity.  Outline the things done by each character studied in the section,  Discuss how the characters make the story flow,  Write a summary about how the main characters make the story flow.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 4.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Readers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Learning to learn is developed as the learner shares ideas on how the characters make the story flow.

 Critical thinking is developed as the learner makes predictions from the title and the section read.

Values:
Responsibility is enhanced as the learner writes a summary based on the main character.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Critical thinking is enhanced as the learner discusses how characters contribute to the flow of the story.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the concept of prediction to their learning in Integrated Science.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify the main characters in a text,
2. explain how the characters make the story flow,
3. make predictions based on the title and the sections read,
4. appreciate the role of characters in the class reader.  Read a section of a class reader and identify the main characters,  Discuss predictions made from the title and the sections read. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative communication modes as they share their views. Allow more time for learners with speech difficulties to express their views. What would you consider when selecting a storybook to read? 36  Participate in a reader’s theatre and read portions of the class reader. Create a conducive environment and adequate space for learners with mobility difficulties and ensure safety for all learners as they perform the activity.  Outline the things done by each character studied in the section,  Discuss how the characters make the story flow,  Write a summary about how the main characters make the story flow.

Remember the key question: What would you consider when selecting a storybook to read?
